internalNote: Per-song meter, key, scripture reference, and text/tune attribution built from a real, authoritative TSV Kevin provided (1991topmatter.tsv, 454 real data rows), cross-checked thoroughly against the existing Library page index before import - several real findings along the way, all handled deliberately rather than silently. (1) Mislabeling pattern, 42 pages: the TSV labels pages like "201b", "235b" etc. as bottom-half split pages (Sort values like "201.2"), but no corresponding top half exists anywhere in the TSV, and the title in every one of these 42 cases matches the Library's own existing BARE page key exactly (e.g. "201b" in the TSV = "Pilgrim", matching the Library's own bare "201" = "Pilgrim") - these are the sole song on their page, not a real split, matching a known failure mode the extraction guide itself explicitly warns against. Mapped to the Library's existing bare keys rather than imported as false new split pages. (2) A real, substantial gap: pages 104-198 (103 real pages, roughly a fifth of the whole book) are completely absent from the TSV - not a labeling issue, genuinely missing data. No Level 3 enrichment exists for this range in this file; it needs a separate batch. (3) Two new pages in the TSV ("25" = Fire Alarm, "24b" = The Young Convert) aren't in the Library's own "complete" page index at all yet - deliberately NOT added here, since expanding an edition's own page index is a real, separate Library-level decision, not something to do silently while building Level 3 enrichment. A third TSV row ("24t") has no data of any kind and was skipped regardless. (4) A real, widespread encoding issue: 68 instances across Text Meter and Scripture Verse used Cyrillic look-alike characters in place of Latin ones (e.g. Cyrillic С instead of Latin C in "C.M.", Cyrillic Е instead of Latin E in "Ecc.") - a clear, mechanical, unambiguous substitution pattern (not genuine ambiguity), normalized back to standard Latin text before import. (5) A likely, unconfirmed transcription typo, NOT corrected: page 278b's ("Traveling Pilgrim") scripture citation reads "Man goeth to his long sought hote" - almost certainly meant to read "home", but left exactly as given rather than guessed at. (6) A real, worth-flagging discrepancy the Level 3 build itself never touches, since title stays Library-owned regardless: the TSV's own First/Second disambiguation numbers for two page pairs appear reversed from the Library's existing, page-order-consistent labeling - "Mount Zion" (Library: page 88b=First, page 220=Second; TSV instead pairs 88b with "Second" and 220 with "First") and "Restoration" (Library: page 271b=First, page 312b=Second; TSV instead pairs 271b with "Second" and 312b with "First"). The Library's own titles were not changed by this import in either case. 451 of the Library's 554 real pages now have real Level 3 enrichment; the remaining 103 (the 104-198 gap) do not yet. A second batch supplemented this file from a real Hymnary.org search-results export (searchResults.csv, 554 rows), per Kevin's explicit instruction to supplement missing schema fields only, never overwrite anything already present. Verified directly before writing: zero existing field values changed. This export uses "a"/"b" suffixes for split pages rather than this project's own "t"/"b" convention - confirmed by cross-checking known titles outside any gap (e.g. its "28a"=Aylesbury and "29a"=Fairfield match this file's own existing 28t/29t exactly), so "a" was mapped to "t", "b" stayed "b". This filled the previously-open 104-198 gap completely (103 new pages, meter/textAttribution/musicAttribution only - this export has no scriptureReference data) and added 249 individual missing fields across 90 of the already-enriched pages. All 554 of the Library's real pages now have at least some Level 3 enrichment, though field completeness still varies by page since neither source covered everything (in particular, scriptureReference is still only populated for pages covered by the original TSV batches).
